findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for, and what problem it solves. Someone who reads only that paragraph could describe the project in a sentence.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository.

findings.text: The header links straight to the next step. The Next steps section then lists prerequisites, the clone and setup commands, and a first command to try (`athena ask "add a changelog"`), so the newcomer knows what to do.
findings.source: Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself

findings.text: Athena's main promise is a commit with the cost and a second model's verdict attached, but the page never shows one. All it shows is a read-only study, so the newcomer has to take that promise on trust.
findings.source: records what each step cost ... get back a commit they can trace to the request, the models, the cost and the verdict

findings.text: The page is titled and built around firstmate, someone else's project, rather than Athena. A newcomer who came to learn about Athena has to scroll past states, transitions t1–t12, design cards ra1–ra6 and 45 claims about a tool they may never use, before reaching Next steps near the bottom.
findings.source: Athena explains how firstmate handles work

findings.text: This link sits in the header with no explanation. A newcomer cannot tell who the "owner" is or whether the link is meant for them.
findings.source: Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision.

findings.text: The state list shows only a name, a tag and claim ids (for example "queued initial"). The meaning of each state is in the glossary, not here. The transition cards also use opaque ids (t1, ra1) that a first-time reader has to cross-reference.
findings.source: States of a piece of work

findings.text: The page is open about a gap: "in scope" is never defined, even though it decides what firstmate may merge by itself. That honesty supports the trust claim, but it leaves a key rule unexplained.
findings.source: in scope ... The cited instruction does not say what makes work in scope, so this page gives no test for it.

findings.text: The page says every statement traces to lines in the source, and the Limits section says "every claim is marked read". This trade-off, however, is marked "(inferred)", so not every statement on the page is backed by a source line.
findings.source: Trade-off: The caller sees an error and must try again, but a stuck holder cannot hang the spawn (inferred).

findings.text: The page does not say which repository the `studies/` folder is in. A newcomer cannot find the source data from this note alone.
findings.source: This page's study id, firstmate-work-handling, is the name of the folder under studies/
